title: Preflight Change Cartography: Predictive Impact Mapping + Safe Rollback Orchestration
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: Recent incidents showed that tuning batching/caching and other runtime knobs can cause subtle regressions that only surface after warmup (higher tail latency) or after KV cache divergence. Rather than purely reactive auto-revert, we want a preflight system that builds an impact map (cartography) for a config change, runs a short synthetic shadow apply with workload-aware prefix warming, predicts economic and correctness regressions, and attaches an automatic rollback plan (soft rollback / hard rollback) if thresholds are crossed.

Goals:
- Produce a change 'cartography' that lists affected call paths, models, routes, and expected sequence-length distributions.
- Run a fast shadow-apply simulation that executes representative synthetic traffic across top N routes to surface regressive latency/cost signals.
- Compute a probabilistic divergence score (0-100) combining correctness regression risk, tail-latency delta, and per-token cost delta.
- If divergence_score > configured threshold OR economic_delta > budget_threshold, do a staged automatic rollback (soft: toggle new cache/batching policy off; hard: revert config).
- Generate a state-reconciliation playbook that contains the exact KV snapshot keys to quarantine, warmup steps, and a follow-up verification run.

Acceptance criteria:
- Cartography generator built and validated against three representative services (text-generation, chat-routing, embeddings).
- Shadow-apply harness that can run in <5 minutes for top 20 routes and return metrics (p95/p99 latency, token cost, output-diff-rate).
- Divergence scorer implemented and unit-tested with synthetic regressions (lossy quantization, disabled prefix cache).
- Automated rollback executor that supports soft rollback and full revert and logs decision rationale to telemetry.
- Reconciliation playbook that replays a warmup sequence to rehydrate KV caches and verifies parity within tolerances.

Design decisions / trade-offs considered:
- Full end-to-end canary vs targeted shadow apply: Canary risks user impact; shadow apply provides safer signal but may miss correlated production anomalies. We choose shadow apply + optional canary escalation only when shadow signals are ambiguous.
- Synthetic workload fidelity vs speed: Use a hybrid: short high-fidelity runs for top N routes + lightweight statistically representative runs for long-tail routes.
- Threshold sensitivity: To avoid noisy rollbacks we use hysteresis and require at least two independent signal types (latency + cost or latency + correctness) before hard revert.

Plan of work (rough):
1) Cartography service (2 pts): parse config change diff, map affected routes/models, estimate sequence-length distribution per route.
2) Shadow runner (3 pts): runner that can replay synthetic traces against a shadow deployment and capture metrics.
3) Divergence scorer (1 pt): combine signals into single score and configurable thresholds.
4) Rollback executor + playbook writer (2 pts): safe soft/hard rollback flows + generate reconciliation steps.

Telemetry & observability:
- New metrics: preflight.divergence_score, preflight.latency_delta, preflight.cost_delta, preflight.correctness_rate.
- Audit log entry for every automated decision with config diff, score breakdown, and PR link.

Security/Compliance: Shadow applies run in isolated namespaces with data-masking for PII. Reconciliation artifacts (KV key lists) are stored encrypted; access audited.

Artifacts / links:
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CFG/Preflight+Change+Cartography
- Shadow runner prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8312
- Runbook draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3cRunbooks
- Design mockups (cartography UI): https://figma.com/file/xyZ-cartography

Notes on scope limits:
- This ticket intentionally excludes global rollout orchestration; it focuses on preflight detection + rollback and producing the reconciliation playbook. Integration with rollout manager will be a follow-on ticket.
